stories.notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and null spec — needs openspec to elaborate requirements and propose AC for this complex cross-platform live-preview feature, then speckit to harden with testability, security, and edge-case criteria. No prior hand-curation to protect.

agentContributions.notes: ACs were empty — derived from the two testable behaviors in the description: (1) auto-update on save without manual refresh, (2) rendering through the same component pipeline as production, across GO/UP/MX brands. Attachment points are useContent (236 callers, central data hook) and ContentstackContext (provides content state to the component tree). Contentstack.io is unreachable at test time; VCs stop at our side of that boundary.

Openspec's AC array was empty; they identified two behaviors in notes (auto-update on save, same component pipeline across brands) and key attachment points (useContent, ContentstackContext). I formalized those two behaviors as AC-1 and AC-2 with Given/When/Then structure. Added AC-3 and AC-4 for connection loss/reconnection edge cases. Added AC-5 for malformed data error handling. Added AC-6 for concurrent edit conflict resolution. Added AC-7 and AC-8 for accessibility (live region announcements, keyboard navigation). Added AC-9 for loading state observability. Added AC-10 and AC-11 for security (credential leakage prevention, authorization). Added AC-12 to ensure brand-specific rendering fidelity is verified distinctly from the pipeline correctness in AC-2. I could not inspect file contents (useContent, ContentstackContext) since tool calls are unavailable; if those files reveal additional error paths or state transitions, further ACs may be warranted.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents contributed non-overlapping value but in an inverted pipeline order. Openspec performed reconnaissance (identified two core behaviors and key attachment points: useContent, ContentstackContext) but produced zero formalized ACs — acceptanceChanged: false, splitCount: 0. Speckit then did the heavy lifting, formalizing 12 ACs from openspec's notes covering core behavior (AC-1/2), edge cases (AC-3/4/5), conflict resolution (AC-6), accessibility (AC-7/8), observability (AC-9), and security (AC-10/11/12). This is substantial coverage, but speckit is intended to review and harden openspec's output, not generate the primary deliverable. Two data integrity concerns: (1) acceptanceChanged is false for both agents despite speckit adding 12 ACs, and (2) the story's acceptanceCriteria array is still empty [], meaning the deltas were not actually applied despite both agents reporting applied: true. Additionally, no story split was proposed despite 12 ACs spanning live preview, error handling, conflict resolution, accessibility, and security across three brands (GO/UP/MX) — this scope likely warrants decomposition. Speckit also noted it could not inspect file contents (useContent, ContentstackContext) due to tool unavailability, so additional error paths or state transitions may be uncovered once those files are reviewed. Human review needed to: verify AC application, assess split candidacy, and confirm no gaps from uninspected source files.
